original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: For any field K and any role count, prove that xI+yA over K[x,y]/(x,y)^2 is unreachable at every finite paid length when A has no K-valued left eigenvector. Give the binary three-role cubic companion and exact finite corroboration.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a changed connector operation with a completed budget. This contribution instead extends the two-role square-zero question of PR4745 to a necessary condition at arbitrary role count in the same formal right-vector alphabet. It is a scoped algebraic side result, not a priced interface.
bottleneck_link: A general-target rank estimate does not imply reachability in the base-field right-vector alphabet. The obstruction rejects a whole family before searching paid words; physical supplier costs are not inferred.
stop_rule: Stop at the first proved multi-role obstruction and its bounded reproducer; leave sufficiency and restored auxiliary roles open.
evidence: Written arbitrary-field and arbitrary-word-length proof; 802816 binary single-coefficient first-zero transition checks, including 150528 invertible cases; direct enumeration excludes 48 of 512 binary three-role pencils; 1536 chronological dirty-input comparisons and two chronology controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Is a base-field eigenvalue sufficient for reachability of xI+yA when n>=3, or do nonsplit invariant factors still obstruct it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The present theorem is a necessary condition only; a complete criterion could avoid unbounded word searches.
open_questions.first_step: Test the three-role direct sum of one scalar block and the companion of t^2+t+1 over F2.
open_questions.blocked_by: The first-zero step supplies one common row but does not recursively control its quotient.

open_questions.question: Can extra roles restored to the identity make an excluded radical pencil reachable?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Physical dirty auxiliary roles change the scalar endpoint from zero to a nonzero projector.
open_questions.first_step: Study diag(xI3+yA,I1) for the displayed cubic companion with the same restricted right vectors.
open_questions.blocked_by: The proof uses a zero full scalar endpoint and does not apply to this padding.
